title: RLS — Row Level Security
summary: JWT = who you are — RLS = which rows you can see — rules on the database itself

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **How to set rules at the database level for which rows each user can see** — **even if there is a mistake in the code**.
- **Why now?** **JWT (JSON Web Token) tells you «who you are»** — **RLS (Row Level Security) tells you «what you are allowed to see» from the data**.
- **What after the lesson?** **You will write one rule:** **the user sees only their own data**.
- **Optional depth:** **for those who want to build real applications**. **You can skip it and come back later**.

sections.heading: Tension — Client A saw Client B's secrets
sections.subtitle: Client A saw Client B's secrets
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Imagine a personal AI learning from each client's notes**. **Another client opened the app and found the first client's secrets in front of them**.
- **Knowing the ID does not mean you can see it**. **And the correct code in 9 places is not enough if you forget the tenth**.
- **The problem:** **security in the code alone is not a last line of defense**.

sections.heading: Core idea — rules determine which rows the user sees
sections.subtitle: Rules determine which rows the user sees
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **JWT verifies your identity**. **RLS Policy applies a filter to every query to the database:** «Return only the rows where `user_id` = me».
- **The filter is within the database itself** — **not just in the application code**.
- **Even if the code in the background forgets the WHERE clause**, **the row guard refuses to show data that does not belong to you**.

sections.heading: Comparison — Security in code vs. Row guard on each row
sections.subtitle: Security in code vs. Row guard on each row
sections.contentMarkdown:
| WHERE in code only | RLS on the database |
|--------------------|----------------|
| **`WHERE user_id = currentUser` in every API**. **Forgot once — a client's secrets were exposed** | **Policy on the table:** `user_id = auth.uid()`. **Any query — even by mistake — returns only the current user's rows** |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two terms to start
sections.subtitle: Two terms to start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **RLS (Row Level Security)** | **Rules on the database itself filter any query before returning results** — **even if the code forgets the filter** | **Chat table:** **Each user sees only their own chats** |
| **Policy** | **The condition applied by the guard on each row** | `USING (user_id = auth.uid())` — **returns rows only for those who opened the app** |

sections.heading: Screenshot block (intent)
sections.contentMarkdown:
**A magic lens for each user:**

The database **is one and contains everyone's data**. **When «Ahmad» requests his chats**, **the Policy filters and returns only his rows** — **as if everyone sees only what belongs to them**.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 0

**Question:** **Table `tasks` — each task has `user_id`. What is the logical condition for each person to see only their tasks?**

**`user_id` of the task = `user_id` of the currently logged-in user**.
Anyone can see any task as long as they have the task ID**.**
Must be an admin to see any task**.**

**Explanation:** **The idea of RLS simply is:** **we link each row to its owner** — **`user_id` in the row = `user_id` from JWT**.

sections.heading: Mission — Rule: the user sees only their own data
sections.subtitle: Rule: the user sees only their own data
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** **You will write a simple Policy for your application** — **not a complete SQL code, just the condition**. **10 minutes**.

**Submission:** **Table name**, **Join field** (`user_id`), **condition in a plain sentence**, **why the rule is important**.

**Evaluation criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Condition correct | 60% | **The condition links the table row to the current user's identity**; **clear table and join field** |
| Reason | 40% | **A sentence explaining why the rule prevents data leakage between users** |
